title: Wisconsin Public Universities: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility, 4 Measured | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Wisconsin public universities stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 34% of 163 sampled PDFs untagged, 2% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Wisconsin: Title II PDF backlog at public universities
body:
Wisconsin has 12 public 4-year universities with 5,000+ students in the federal IPEDS directory. Public universities are covered by the ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H), and most are part of state government, which puts them on the April 26, 2027 compliance date. Web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to Wisconsin?

Yes. Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act is federal law and covers every state and local government in every state: Wisconsin's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts. The 2024 web rule adds technical requirements for their websites, apps and the documents they post (WCAG 2.1 Level AA). Its compliance date depends on population: April 26, 2027 for governments serving 50,000 or more people (every state government included), April 26, 2028 for smaller ones and for special districts. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these institutions link from their main websites. This page summarizes Wisconsin as a whole. It does not name or rank individual institutions. See the national university page for the method.

Wisconsin at a glance

  • 4 of 12 institutions measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). The rest blocked automated visitors, host documents on other systems, or had too few PDFs to sample; that is not a clean result.
  • 163 PDFs analyzed. 34.4% had no accessibility tags, higher than the national figure of 26.7%. 2.5% were scanned images with no usable text, and 23.9% did not declare a document language.
  • 0 of 12 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured institution has roughly 497 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured institutions that is on the order of 3,000 pages.
  • 56% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for a Wisconsin university

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, no reading order and no table structure. A scanned PDF gives it nothing at all. Both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA (for example 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, and for scans 1.1.1 Non-text Content), and both are common in catalogs, policies, forms and board materials.

Not every old PDF has to be fixed. The rule exempts archived web content and preexisting conventional electronic documents unless they are currently used to apply for, access or participate in a service. The practical order is usually: fix the export settings so new documents are born accessible, remediate forms and anything people use to get a service, and move true archives to a clearly marked archive section. Our ADA Title II PDF guide walks through it.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals, not a conformance evaluation. An automated check can show that a PDF fails; it cannot show that a PDF conforms. Estimates are scaled from samples, and a few very long documents can move a number a lot. The full method is on the national Backlog Index page.

Per-institution data

The Wisconsin workbook lists every targeted public university in the state, with PDFs found and estimated, untagged and scanned shares, recent-document share, estimated pages failing basic checks and days to the compliance date. It is built for remediation firms, consultants and agencies planning work.

Per-institution rows for Wisconsin are available on request: email us.
